items.stem: On the School Data Owners page, who can assign a delegate for a school?

options.text: The principal, who owns the school's data
A central administration team that processes requests
Any signed-in SDM user
The HRAD system of record, automatically

items.explanation: In SDM's RACI self-serve model the owner assigns the delegate. For a school that owner is the principal.

misconceptions.b: The self-serve model deliberately removes a central team from the loop — the owner decides.
misconceptions.c: Assignment is the owner's right, not any user's.
misconceptions.d: HRAD is the system of record for school records; it doesn't assign delegates.

items.stem: What two responsibilities can a delegate be assigned for their area?

options.text: Maintaining the area's supplemental data and managing its SPO (SharePoint Online) site
Creating new schools and deleting closed ones
Editing the HRAD system of record and the AuditLog
Approving budgets and signing contracts

items.explanation: A delegate is assigned to maintain the area's supplemental data and to manage its SharePoint Online site in the owner's capacity.

misconceptions.b: Creating/deleting schools happens upstream in HRAD, not via a Data-Owner delegate.
misconceptions.c: The system of record and AuditLog aren't edit surfaces a delegate manages.
misconceptions.d: Those are organizational duties, not the data/SPO responsibilities SDM delegates.

items.stem: The three Data-Owner pages — Department, School, and Functional Site — differ primarily in what?

options.text: Their scope and owning role (manager / principal / owner); the mechanism is the same
Whether edits are audited in DDH
Whether they use Entra (AAD) at all
Whether a delegate can be assigned at all

items.explanation: All three work the same way; only the scope (Department/School/Functional Site) and owning role (manager/principal/owner) change.

misconceptions.b: All SDM edits write to DDH with audit — that doesn't distinguish the pages.
misconceptions.c: Authorization across SDM rests on Entra DA-* groups regardless of the page.
misconceptions.d: Delegate assignment is the shared mechanism on all three pages.

items.stem: A department manager is overloaded and wants someone else to keep the department's supplemental data current and run its SharePoint site. Under SDM's model, what should happen?

options.text: The manager assigns a delegate on Department Data Owners; the delegate then maintains the data and the SPO site
The manager files a ticket so a central team takes over the department's data
The data goes unmaintained until HRAD pushes an update
Ownership transfers permanently to whoever edits the record next

items.explanation: The RACI self-serve model lets the owner assign a delegate to carry the data-maintenance and SPO responsibility, rather than handing it to a central team.

misconceptions.b: The self-serve model exists precisely so this isn't routed to a central team.
misconceptions.c: HRAD supplies system-of-record fields, not the supplemental data a delegate maintains.
misconceptions.d: Delegation is an explicit assignment by the owner, not an accident of who edits last.

items.stem: A teacher complains they were never made a delegate for their functional site, even though the owner intended it. Where would you confirm who was actually assigned?

options.text: In DDH, where the assignment is recorded with CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit (reversible via soft delete)
Only by asking the central access team, since SDM keeps no record
In SDM's own separate source of truth, which is independent of DDH
Nowhere — delegate assignments are not tracked

items.explanation: Delegate assignments are edits like any other, so they write to DDH with CreatedBy/UpdatedBy audit and a soft-delete flag, making them attributable and reversible.

misconceptions.b: The self-serve model has no central team owning this, and SDM does record the change in DDH.
misconceptions.c: SDM holds no separate source of truth; authoritative data lives in DDH.
misconceptions.d: All SDM edits, including delegation, carry an audit trail.

items.stem: In one or two sentences, describe SDM's RACI self-serve model for Data Owners, and give a concrete example of an owner assigning a delegate.
rubric: States responsibility sits with the owner (manager/principal/owner) or their delegate, not a central team
States the delegate maintains the area's supplemental data and manages its SPO (SharePoint Online) site
Gives a valid example, e.g. a principal assigning an office administrator as a delegate for the school
items.sampleAnswer: Responsibility for an area's supplemental data sits with its owner — the manager, principal, or functional-site owner — or with a delegate the owner assigns, not a central team. For example, a principal can assign an office administrator as a delegate so that person maintains the school's supplemental data and manages its SharePoint Online site.
